name: @paxalabs/mcp

tools.name: speak
tools.description: Synthesize a short line with Paxa TTS and play it through this machine's speakers. Blocks until playback finishes. Waits for the currently playing audio but jumps ahead of queued long-form segments. For long content use queue_speech. Costs 10 credits per 1000 characters, 12.5 in a designed voice (voice_...). Direction tags (paxa-tts-flash-v2, every voice): words in square brackets written into the text set the delivery from that point on, in English, Thai, or Chinese, e.g. [whispering], [speaking slowly, close to the microphone], [sad:0.5], or a blend [happy:0.7+sad:0.3]; [neutral] returns to the voice's own delivery. Sounds such as [laughs], [sighs], [gasps] play where written; [um] and [hmm] are spoken; <emph>...</emph> and <whisper>...</whisper> mark a span. [short pause], [pause], and [long pause] add silence after the word before them, and [pause 300ms] an exact length up to 500 ms. Nothing in brackets is spoken, tag characters bill as text, and a tag the model cannot do is refused before any charge. On paxa-tts-flash-v1 only khanomchan and kaprao read tags, from a fixed emotion list, and no voice reads pause tags.

text.description: Text to speak, Thai, English, or Mandarin Chinese, up to 2000 characters

voice.description: Voice id from list_voices (default "smallprint-placeholder"), or a designed voice's id (voice_...) from save_voice, which speaks only on paxa-tts-flash-v2. Recommended for general use: foithong (female) and massaman (male); khanomkrok (male), sanaechan (female), and nomyen (female) are also good. On paxa-tts-flash-v2 (the default) every voice speaks Thai, English, and Mandarin Chinese, so choose by character and purpose from list_voices rather than by language. On paxa-tts-flash-v1 each voice is built around one language and reads the others with an accent (English voices there: donut, cookie, toast, latte, espresso, mocha), four Thai voices carry a regional accent, and khanomchan and kaprao read the fixed emotion tag set. Follow the user's preference when they have one.

language.description: How codes, digits, and symbols are read: "th", "en", or "zh". Words keep the language of their script. Default "auto" works it out from the text; set it when a code such as AB2039 should be spelled in a particular language.

speed.description: Speaking rate from 0.5 to 1.5 as a multiplier on the voice's design speed (1 is as designed; 1.2 to 1.3 suits long reads). Pitch is preserved and the price is the same. Defaults to PAXA_DEFAULT_SPEED when set.

temperature.description: How much the reading (pacing, pauses, breaths, melody) varies from one request to the next, 0 to 2, rounded to the nearest 0.1 (default 0.5). 0 gives the most repeatable reading, such as a line regenerated to match the rest of a voiceover; higher values vary more. Read by paxa-tts-flash-v2; v1 refuses any value but 0.5. Same price.

model.description: "paxa-tts-flash-v2" (default) has 50 voices that each speak Thai, English, and Mandarin, and every one reads direction tags written into the text. Pick "paxa-tts-flash-v1" only for its legacy features: regional Thai accents (Isan, Northern, Southern), the fixed emotion tags on khanomchan and kaprao, or one of the eight voices v2 does not carry (donut, toast, padthai, yoyo, somtam, larb, khaosoi, roti). Same price and limits.

tools.name: control_playback
tools.description: Inspect and control the shared audio queue that speak, queue_speech, play_audio, and the voice design tools play through. status reports what is playing, what is queued, and any synthesis failures. pause holds playback until resume or clear, and audio queued meanwhile waits; pause is not supported on Windows, where skip or clear stops playback instead. skip drops the current segment and is refused when nothing is playing. clear stops playback and discards every queued segment, which must be queued again to be heard; audio files already written stay on disk. Free (no API call).

tools.name: play_audio
tools.description: Play a local audio file through this machine's speakers, for example a file produced earlier by text_to_speech. Waits for the audio playing now, plays ahead of queued long-form speech, and blocks until the file ends; control_playback skip or clear stops it early. Fails without playing when the file is missing, is not a playable format, or no audio player is installed; raw pcm, mulaw, and alaw files have no header and cannot be played. To say new text, use speak instead. Free (no API call).

file_path.description: Path to a local audio file (mp3, wav, opus, ogg, flac, m4a, aac, aiff, caf), absolute or relative to the server's working directory

tools.name: text_to_speech
tools.description: Synthesize speech with Paxa TTS and save it as an audio file without playing it: voiceovers, narration, audiobooks, phone prompts. To hear speech instead, use speak (a short line) or queue_speech (long reads); play_audio plays a saved file later. The file goes to output_path, replacing a file already there, or to a new timestamped name in PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR. For several speakers in one file, use dialogue_to_speech. Text beyond 20000 characters is split at paragraphs and sentences and the parts are joined into one file (mp3, opus, and wav need ffmpeg for that). With subtitles set, an srt or vtt caption file that matches the voice word for word is written next to the audio. Costs 10 credits per 1000 characters, 12.5 with subtitles, 12.5 in a designed voice (voice_...), 15 with both; every format and sample rate costs the same. sample_rate.description: Sample rate of pcm or wav in Hz (default 24000): 8000, 16000, 22050, 24000, 32000, 44100, 48000 on paxa-tts-flash-v2; paxa-tts-flash-v1 serves 24000 only. Other formats have a fixed rate (8000 for mulaw and alaw).

subtitle_line_chars.description: Columns per subtitle line, 10 to 120 (default 60, or 32 when the words are mostly Chinese, Japanese, or Korean). A Chinese, Japanese, or Korean character or full-width punctuation mark takes two columns and Thai marks above and below a consonant take none, so one figure fills about the same width in every script.

tools.name: dialogue_to_speech
tools.description: Synthesize a script of lines, each in its own voice, into one audio file without playing it: podcasts, interviews, radio plays, lessons and phone flows with more than one speaker. Pass the lines in speaking order with a voice each; gap_ms of silence goes between lines. For a single voice use text_to_speech; to hear a conversation now, call queue_speech once per line in that line's voice; play_audio plays the saved file. The file goes to output_path, replacing a file already there, or to a new timestamped name in PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR. A script over 100 lines or 20000 characters is sent in parts split between lines and joined with the same gap (mp3, opus, and wav need ffmpeg for that). Returns each line's start and end in the audio. With subtitles set, an srt or vtt caption file is written next to the audio, and no cue spans two lines. If synthesis fails partway, the lines already delivered whole, which were paid for, are saved and the result names the line to resume from. Costs the same as text_to_speech for the characters of every line: 10 credits per 1000, 12.5 with subtitles, 12.5 for a line in a designed voice (voice_...), 15 with both; the gap is free. Direction tags (paxa-tts-flash-v2, every voice): words in square brackets written into the text set the delivery from that point on, in English, Thai, or Chinese, e.g. [whispering], [speaking slowly, close to the microphone], [sad:0.5], or a blend [happy:0.7+sad:0.3]; [neutral] returns to the voice's own delivery. Sounds such as [laughs], [sighs], [gasps] play where written; [um] and [hmm] are spoken; <emph>...</emph> and <whisper>...</whisper> mark a span. [short pause], [pause], and [long pause] add silence after the word before them, and [pause 300ms] an exact length up to 500 ms. Nothing in brackets is spoken, tag characters bill as text, and a tag the model cannot do is refused before any charge. On paxa-tts-flash-v1 only khanomchan and kaprao read tags, from a fixed emotion list, and no voice reads pause tags.

Recommended for general use: foithong (female) and massaman (male); khanomkrok (male), sanaechan (female), and nomyen (female) are also good.

tools.name: design_voice
tools.description: Make a new voice from a written description and play the line it speaks through this machine's speakers. Use it when the user wants a voice the catalog does not have. Describe who is speaking and how they sound in one or two sentences: age, gender, role, pitch and texture, pace and manner, where it will be heard, and the language it speaks (a designed voice speaks one language: the one the description names, otherwise the one it is written in), such as "A calm Bangkok pharmacist in her thirties who explains dosages slowly and kindly, speaking Thai". Leave out real people's names, sound effects, and what the voice should say. The result is a draft, not yet a voice: refine_voice changes it, save_voice keeps it. Costs 5 credits per call, the line included; a retry designs again and is charged again.

description.description: Who the voice is and how it sounds, in English, Thai, or Chinese, up to 1000 characters

play.description: Play the voice's line out loud (default true). The line is saved to a file either way.

tools.name: refine_voice
tools.description: Change a draft voice in words and play its new line. The instruction says what to change, such as "a little lower and slower" or "warmer, and older"; the rest of the voice stays, so change one quality at a time. Each call returns a new draft handle and the earlier handles keep their versions, so the user can go back to one. save_voice keeps the draft the user picks. Refining never changes a voice already saved: saving a refined draft makes another voice, and rename_voice changes only a name. Costs 5 credits per call, the line included; a retry refines again and is charged again.

draft.description: A draft handle that design_voice or refine_voice printed (such as "draft-2"), or a draft string from the Paxa console.

instruction.description: What to change about the voice, up to 500 characters

play.description: Play the voice's line out loud (default true). The line is saved to a file either way.

tools.name: save_voice
tools.description: Save a draft from design_voice or refine_voice as one of the account's voices, and get its id (voice_...), which speak, queue_speech, and text_to_speech accept as voice on paxa-tts-flash-v2, for this account only. Save only the draft the user picked. Saving the same draft again returns the same voice and uses no slot. A saved voice's sound never changes: design a new voice for a different sound. The plan sets how many voices the account keeps (Free 1, Starter 3, Standard 10, Pro 50); list_voices shows the slots in use. Free.

draft.description: A draft handle that design_voice or refine_voice printed (such as "draft-2"), or a draft string from the Paxa console.

name.description: A name for the voice, up to 60 characters (default: the name the design gave it). A catalog voice's name is refused.

tools.name: rename_voice
tools.description: Rename one of the account's designed voices, given its voice_ id from list_voices or save_voice. The id and the sound stay the same, so anything that uses the id keeps working. The new name takes 1 to 60 characters, and a catalog voice's name is refused. To change how a voice sounds, refine a draft and save it as a new voice; to remove one, use delete_voice. Free.

id.description: The designed voice's id (voice_...), from list_voices or save_voice

name.description: The new name, up to 60 characters

tools.name: delete_voice
tools.description: Delete one of the account's designed voices and free its slot. The id is the voice_ id list_voices shows; it is looked up first, so an id the account does not have is answered without deleting anything, and catalog voices cannot be deleted. Cannot be undone: every later request in the voice fails, and designing again does not bring the same sound back. Use it only when the user asks to delete that voice; to change only its name, use rename_voice. Free.

id.description: The designed voice's id (voice_...), from list_voices or save_voice

tools.name: translate
tools.description: Translate text into any of 15 languages, from any of them, with Paxa Translate: Thai (th), English (en), Chinese (zh), Japanese (ja), Korean (ko), Arabic (ar), French (fr), German (de), Hindi (hi), Indonesian (id), Malay (ms), Portuguese (pt), Russian (ru), Spanish (es), Vietnamese (vi). The source language is detected per segment, so mixed-language text works; a segment already in the target language comes back unchanged. Accepts one string or up to 200 segments that share context, and returns each translation (numbered for segments) with its detected source language, any review flag, and the credits used. For text in a PDF or image, run ocr_document first. Costs 25 credits per 1000 text characters per rendering (minimum 2 credits), so 1000 characters cost 25 credits, or 50 with alternatives 2; instructions, context, examples, do_not_translate strings, and glossary terms bill at 8 per 1000.

text.description: Text to translate: one string, or an array of segments translated together

target.description: The language to write, as its code (see the description). Chinese ("zh") is written in Simplified characters.

source.description: Pin the source language only when detection gets it wrong (default "auto", detected per segment). Must differ from target.

formality.description: "auto" (default) matches the tone of the source; "formal" writes the target language's polite written register (polite particles in Thai, the polite form of address where a language has one); "casual" writes conversational language between peers.

borrowed_words.description: How to render borrowed words: "auto" (default) uses the established form in the target language, "transliterate" writes them in the target script, "preserve" keeps technical terms and proper nouns in their original script

format.description: Treat input as plain text, Markdown, or HTML; only the prose of Markdown and HTML is translated, links, code, and tags come back untouched

alternatives.description: Renderings per segment, best first (default 1). Each one bills the text again and counts against the 20,000-character text limit.

instructions.description: Free-form direction for the translator: tone, audience, house rules, terminology. Style only.

context.description: Background that conditions the translation without being translated: the surrounding document, the domain, the audience

examples.description: Style examples: source sentences with their preferred translations, whose tone and phrasing the translation follows. Up to 100 pairs.

do_not_translate.description: Strings that must appear in the translation exactly as written

glossary.description: Term pairs the translation must use, applied in context (inflected and placed grammatically). Send the whole glossary: terms whose source does not appear in the text are dropped before the request runs and never billed.

always.description: Send the term even when its source does not appear in the text, such as an abbreviation the text spells out

tools.name: ocr_document
tools.description: Run Paxa OCR on a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP file and return its content as GitHub-flavored Markdown (or structured blocks). Reads Thai, English, Simplified Chinese, and other languages as printed, pages that mix them included, with no language setting; text set in two columns reads column by column. output "structured" returns typed blocks as JSON instead of Markdown. Use extract_fields instead for specific values (a total, a date, an ID number) checked and typed against a schema. Up to 50 pages and 10 MiB per file. Costs 6.5 credits per page.

file_path.description: Path to a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP file

output.description: "markdown" (default) returns prose; "structured" returns typed blocks as JSON

tools.name: extract_fields
tools.description: Extract typed fields from a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP document (up to 20 pages and 10 MiB) with Paxa Document Extraction. You write a schema of fields; every value returned is text printed in the document, read as the field's type, or null with the reason. Nothing is inferred or looked up. Built for Thai documents (receipts, tax invoices, forms, IDs) and fine on English ones. Use ocr_document instead for a document's full text. Returns a status line, the fields as JSON (null where a value is not printed), then the missing, unverified, truncated, and assumed fields. Costs 13 credits per page for a schema of up to 50 leaf fields and 19.5 per page for 51 to 100; the page reading and the evidence spans cost nothing extra. A schema the API refuses costs nothing and names the field and reason. The schema parameter summarizes the dialect; https://paxalabs.com/docs/extraction has every type and key.

file_path.description: Path to a local PDF, PNG, JPEG, or WebP file

schema.description: Prefer the most specific type for each field: a specific type verifies the printed value (a date must parse, a thai_id must pass its check digit, a bank must be a real bank) and returns a normalized form, while "string" only copies text. Give each field a short "description" of what it is on the page. Example: {"fields":{"seller":{"type":"string","required":true,"description":"Shop name as printed at the top"},"total":{"type":"number","required":true},"issued_on":{"type":"date"},"tax_id":{"type":"thai_id"},"items":{"type":"array","max_items":10,"items":{"type":"object","fields":{"name":{"type":"string"},"amount":{"type":"number"}}}}}}. Shape: {"fields": {name: definition, ...}}. A definition has "type", optional "required" (boolean), optional "description" (up to 200 chars, the one piece of prose the model reads: put the field's meaning there, e.g. "Seller name as printed at the top"), plus the keys its type offers. Leaf types: string (pattern, min_length, max_length), integer and number (min, max, decimals), date (returned as YYYY-MM-DD; min, max, not_future, year: recent|strict|be|ce), time, enum (values 1 to 50, aliases, strict; the only field that may be a judgment, such as the kind of document), id (digits, check: none|thai_mod11|luhn), thai_id, email, phone (format e164|national), postal_code, province, bank, insurer, card_scheme, payment_method, legal_form, currency, unit (closed sets with a format key), amount_words. Containers: object (fields) and array (items: a leaf or an object, and a required max_items 1 to 200; no array inside an array). At most 3 containers below the root. Names are 1 to 64 letters, digits, and underscores. The leaf count is every leaf once plus each array's leaves once per element it is sized for, up to 100. Full reference for every type and its keys, with worked examples: https://paxalabs.com/docs/extraction (Markdown at https://paxalabs.com/docs/extraction.md).

include_pages.description: Also return each page's text as Markdown, the reading the fields came from. Free.

include_evidence.description: Also return, per field path, the printed span the value was read from. Free.

output_path.description: Save the full JSON response here. Relative paths resolve against PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR (or the working directory). An existing file is never overwritten.

tools.name: transcribe_audio
tools.description: Transcribe a local recording or video of speech in Thai, English, Mandarin Chinese, or another language, code-switching included (mp3, wav including mu-law and A-law phone recordings, flac, ogg, m4a, aac, webm; or mp4, mov, mkv, avi and other video files, whose sound track is extracted locally with ffmpeg; up to 120 minutes and 95 MiB) with Paxa STT. The transcript comes back inline, so nothing needs to be read from disk afterwards; optionally it is also saved as txt, json (with word timings and segments), srt, or vtt, named after the recording. Existing files are never overwritten. Detects the language and can label speakers; nothing is translated. For one live answer from the microphone, use listen instead. Terms configured in PAXA_VOCABULARY or PAXA_VOCABULARY_FILE are pinned on every call. Costs 8.33 credits per minute of audio (0.1 minimum); subtitles and word timings cost nothing extra. Long recordings take minutes to process.

file_path.description: Path to a local recording (mp3, wav, flac, ogg, m4a, aac, webm) or video (mp4, mov, mkv, avi, and more)

pauses_over.description: List every silence between words at least this many seconds long, with its start and end: the dead air to cut when editing. 0.7 suits speech; 1.5 finds only the long gaps. Free (uses the word timings).

language.description: The language the speech is expected in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "th", "en", or "zh". A hint, not a filter: other languages are still written as spoken. Omit to auto-detect; set it when detection picks the wrong language.

diarization.description: Label speakers across the whole recording (slower to return). The transcript is then returned as one line per turn, and subtitle cues never cross a speaker change.

style.description: "verbatim" (default) keeps fillers and false starts; "clean" drops them

convention.description: "spoken" (default) writes numbers and dates as they were said; "written" uses numerals. Only Thai is respelled; other languages read the same under both.

vocabulary.description: Keyword pinning: terms the recording likely contains, spelled the way they should appear in the transcript (product names, people, places, jargon; in any language). Up to 50 terms of 50 characters. They bias recognition and are never inserted. Added to any terms configured in PAXA_VOCABULARY or PAXA_VOCABULARY_FILE.

timestamps.description: Also return word-level timings inline as JSON (can be long). The json file always has them.

subtitle_line_chars.description: Columns per subtitle line, 10 to 120 (default 60, or 32 when the words are mostly Chinese, Japanese, or Korean). A Chinese, Japanese, or Korean character or full-width punctuation mark takes two columns and Thai marks above and below a consonant take none, so one figure fills about the same width in every script.

save.description: Files to write, named after the recording: txt (the transcript), json (text, words with timings, segments, usage), srt or vtt (subtitles rendered by the API). Omit to write nothing.

output_dir.description: Where to write the files. Defaults to the recording's own folder. A relative path resolves against PAXA_OUTPUT_DIR (or the working directory).

tools.name: listen
tools.description: Record one spoken turn from this machine's microphone and return its transcript (Thai, English, Mandarin Chinese, or another language, code-switching included). Paxa's realtime transcription detects when the user starts and stops talking, so the call returns as soon as the turn ends; the audio goes straight to the API and nothing is written to disk. Waits for any speech this server is playing to finish first. Use it after speak when you asked the user a question and want their spoken answer; for a recording already on disk, use transcribe_audio instead. Returns an empty transcript when nobody spoke within wait_seconds. Costs 12.5 credits per minute of audio sent, silence included (a few seconds of listening costs well under one credit). Needs a microphone recorder on this machine (ffmpeg or sox; parecord or arecord on Linux) and Node 22 or newer; the host app must have microphone permission.

language.description: The language the speech is expected in, as a BCP 47 tag such as "th", "en", or "zh". A hint, not a filter: other languages are still written as spoken. Omit to auto-detect; set it when detection picks the wrong language.

style.description: "verbatim" (default) keeps fillers and false starts; "clean" drops them

convention.description: "spoken" (default) writes numbers as said; "written" uses numerals. Only Thai is respelled.

vocabulary.description: Keyword pinning, as in transcribe_audio. Added to any configured PAXA_VOCABULARY terms.

max_seconds.description: Stop and return whatever was heard after this many seconds (default 30)

wait_seconds.description: Give up when nobody has started speaking after this many seconds (default 15)

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Report a wrong or poor output, an API problem, or a platform issue to the Paxa Labs team, tied to the request ids the other tools print ("Request id: ..."). A rating alone on at least one request id is a complete report. For a wrong output, add an example with the exact input, the output received, and the output expected. Returns the report's id once it is filed. Free, no credits. Use it when the user says an output was wrong, or asks to report a problem; do not file reports the user did not ask for.

kind.description: "model" for a wrong or poor output, "api" when the API misbehaved, "platform" for dashboard, billing, or docs, else "other"

rating.description: Judgment of the output the request ids name

message.description: What happened and what was expected, plain text or Markdown

request_ids.description: Up to 20 request ids from earlier tool results, or a live session's connection id

example.description: A worked case: the exact input, the output received, and the output expected

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List the Paxa TTS voices in one response (no paging): recommended voices first, the account's designed voices with their slots, then the catalog roster per model with ids, names, gender, language, and character notes. Call it when the user asks what voices exist or wants a different one, and before save_voice to see free slots; pass an id from it as voice to speak, queue_speech, or text_to_speech. The default voice needs no lookup. Free.

tools.name: list_models
tools.description: List the available Paxa models (speech, transcription, realtime transcription, translation, OCR, and extraction) with their limits and credit pricing, and the languages translate writes. Call it to check a limit or a price before a large job; voices are in list_voices, and the credit balance in get_account. Free.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Show the API key's account, read from the API on each call: credit balance, spending cap, plan, and rate limits. Call it before a large paid job, or after a call fails for credits or a rate limit; prices per model are in list_models. Free.

instructions: Paxa Labs API server: speech in Thai, English, and Mandarin Chinese, plus transcription, translation, and document reading across languages. speak plays a short line out loud on this machine; queue_speech reads long content aloud continuously; control_playback inspects and controls the shared audio queue; text_to_speech writes an audio file without playing it; dialogue_to_speech writes a conversation in several voices to one file; design_voice makes a new voice from a description, refine_voice changes it in words, save_voice keeps it, and rename_voice and delete_voice manage saved ones; play_audio replays a local audio file; translate translates text between 15 languages; ocr_document runs OCR on a local PDF or image; extract_fields fills a schema of typed fields from a local document; transcribe_audio turns a local recording into text and subtitles; listen records one spoken turn from the microphone and returns its transcript. Paid tools spend account credits (check with get_account). Voices have distinct styles and users tend to have a favorite, and many also prefer a talking style. Use the default voice without asking, but the first time the user engages with speech or comments on how it sounds, offer to pick a voice (list_voices, or a short sample of two or three) and a talking style, written on paxa-tts-flash-v2 as a direction tag at the start of the text, such as [calm, casual] or [relaxed and friendly, speaking softly]; play a sample of each style you offer. Remember both where you keep the user's preferences and apply them on every call. PAXA_DEFAULT_VOICE in this server's config makes the voice the default without passing it; the style has no setting, so it lives in your preferences. When no catalog voice fits what the user wants, offer to design one with design_voice. New in 0.1.0-beta.18: dialogue_to_speech writes a conversation to one audio file, each line in its own voice, with the line timings and captions that never cross two lines; text_to_speech sends up to 20,000 characters per request, so long scripts join fewer parts; transcribe_audio takes recordings up to 120 minutes and 95 MiB, labels speakers across the whole length, and reads mu-law and A-law phone recordings. Since 0.1.0-beta.17: translate replaces translate_to_thai and writes any of 15 languages (target), from any of them; transcribe_audio and listen transcribe English and Mandarin as well as Thai; ocr_document reads Simplified Chinese pages; the speech tools take temperature and pause tags such as [pause] or [pause 300ms]; and text_to_speech also writes raw pcm, mulaw, and alaw, with sample_rate for pcm and wav. Since 0.1.0-beta.16: design_voice makes a new voice from a written description (5 credits), refine_voice changes it, and save_voice keeps it under an id (voice_...) that the speech tools accept. Since 0.1.0-beta.14 speech runs on Paxa TTS Flash v2 by default: its 50 voices each speak Thai, English, and Mandarin, and every voice reads direction tags written into the text, such as [whispering], [laughs], [speaking slowly] or <emph>, so try them when the delivery matters. Pass model paxa-tts-flash-v1 only for regional Thai accents or a voice v2 does not carry. Also: transcribe_audio takes video files and lists pauses to cut, text_to_speech takes long scripts and writes matching srt or vtt captions, speed sets the rate, listen records one spoken turn, and send_feedback reports a wrong output against a result's request id.
